docs.title: A Security Analyst Cockpit for Modern Security Cyber Operations 🛡️🐺
Overview 🔎
docs.text:
SCOUT is a unified, Obsidian-powered knowledge system designed to serve as the cockpit for Security Analysts working inside modern Security Cyber Operations Centers.

Unlike flat note-taking tools like OneNote, SCOUT brings together:

  • Atomic notetaking 🧩
  • Artifact storage 📁
  • Graph-based relationships 🔗
  • Cross-entity navigation 🗺️

This enables analysts to think and work the way investigations unfold—through relationships, pivots, and interconnected context.

SCOUT is the parent framework for two integrated subsystems:

  • CIPHER – Cyber Threat Intelligence
  • ITID – Incident Type Identification Digits (taxonomy)

Together, they form a cohesive, durable, analyst-centric knowledge architecture.

docs.title: Purpose 🎯
docs.text:
SCOUT exists to:

  • Provide analysts with a central cockpit for SOC activity
  • Replace static note silos with relational knowledge structures
  • Preserve operational knowledge as it accumulates
  • Enable rapid pivoting between related entities
  • Support consistent, structured documentation across the SOC

docs.title: What SCOUT Is 🧭
docs.text:
SCOUT is:

  • A security analyst cockpit for SOC workflows
  • A unified knowledge system for operational cyber activity
  • A graph-enabled explorer of SOC entity relationships
  • A repository for atomic notes and artifacts
  • A structured environment for documenting:
  • Incidents
  • Alerts
  • Observations
  • Detections
  • Procedures
  • TTPs
  • Telemetry references
  • An extensible Obsidian-based framework
  • The overarching ecosystem for CIPHER and ITID

docs.title: What SCOUT Is Not 🚫
docs.text:
SCOUT is not:

  • A SIEM
  • A ticketing or case management system
  • An automation or orchestration platform
  • A detection engine
  • Multi-tenant out of the box

docs.title: Audience 👤
docs.text:
SCOUT is built for:

  • SOC Analysts
  • Incident Responders
  • Threat Hunters
  • CTI Analysts
  • Security Engineers needing structured documentation

Especially those transitioning away from tools like OneNote who require:

  • Better structure
  • Better relationships
  • Better long-term retention

docs.title: Problems SCOUT Solves 🧠💡
docs.text:
• Knowledge loss from flat, siloed tools
  • Lack of pivot capability between related SOC data
  • Tribal knowledge accumulation
  • No atomic documentation model for SOC work
  • No cockpit-style visibility into SOC activities
  • No relational structure linking incidents → alerts → entities → artifacts
  • Inconsistent analyst documentation
  • Difficult onboarding due to scattered information
  • Poor continuity across shifts and investigations
  • Notes that cannot scale from individual to team
  • Difficulty performing cross-entity analysis

docs.title: SCOUT Entity Model 🗂️
docs.text:
SCOUT manages entities such as:

  • Incidents
  • Alerts
  • Observations
  • TTPs
  • Assets & Users
  • IOCs
  • Vulnerabilities
  • Procedures & Playbooks
  • Detection analytics
  • Investigation journals
  • Telemetry references
  • Knowledge references

Through CIPHER:

  • Threat actors
  • Malware
  • Campaigns

docs.title: Relationship to CIPHER 🔮
docs.text:
CIPHER is a subset module of SCOUT, fully dedicated to:

  • Threat actor tracking
  • Malware profiling
  • Campaign analysis
  • Intelligence-driven TTP mapping

SCOUT = operational breadth CIPHER = adversary depth

docs.title: Relationship to ITID 🏷️
docs.text:
ITID is the taxonomic backbone of the SCOUT ecosystem:

  • Classifies incidents
  • Normalizes SOC data
  • Structures relationships across entities

docs.title: Key Features ✨
docs.text:
• Atomic note design
  • Rich graph relationship mapping
  • Unified artifact storage
  • Template-driven workflows
  • Obsidian plugin ecosystem support
  • Integration with CIPHER and ITID subsystems
  • Clean and extensible folder structure

docs.title: Design Philosophy 🧱
docs.text:
1. Everything is an entity
  2. Every entity is atomic
  3. Atomic entities form networks
  4. Analysts navigate via pivots, not folders
  5. Structure creates consistency
  6. Relationships create insight

docs.title: How SCOUT Works ⚙️
docs.text: 1. Create an Entity – generate an atomic note 2. Capture Atomic Information – keep it scoped and precise 3. Attach Artifacts – logs, screenshots, configs, evidence 4. Link Relationships – incidents, alerts, IOCs, TTPs 5. Explore the Graph – visualize context 6. Build the Cockpit – SCOUT grows stronger with every note

docs.title: Cloning the SCOUT repository
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the main page of the SCOUT GitHub repository.
  2. Above the list of files, click <> Code.
  3. Copy the URL for the repository.
    • To clone the repository using HTTPS, under "HTTPS", click .
    • To clone the repository using an SSH key, including a certificate issued by your organization's SSH certificate authority, click SSH, then click .
    • To clone the repository using GitHub CLI, click GitHUb CLI, then click .
  1. Open Git Bash
  2. Change the current working directory to the location where you want the cloned directory.
  3. Type git clone, and then paste the URL you copied in Step 3. 
    git clone https://github.com/kcyerrid/SCOUT
  4. Press Enter to create your local clone.

docs.title: Installing Obsidian
docs.text:
The core engine behind SCOUT is Obsidian, which is supported on Windows, MacOS, and Linux.

Obsidian is available for all major desktop and mobile platforms. These are all the supported ways to download and install Obsidian.

docs.title: Install Obsidian on Windows
docs.text:
1. Open your browser and go to Download Obsidian.
  2. Under Windows, click Universal to download the installation file.
  3. Open the installation file and follow the instructions.
  4. Open Obsidian the same way you would open any other application.

docs.title: Install Obsidian on macOS
docs.text:
1. Open your browser and go to Download Obsidian.
  2. Under macOS, click Universal to download the installation file.
  3. Open the installation file.
  4. In the window that opens, drag Obsidian to the Applications folder.
  5. Open Obsidian the same way you would open any other application.

docs.title: Install Obsidian on Linux
docs.text: If you use Linux, you can install Obsidian in several ways. Follow the instructions for the packaging system that you're using.

docs.title: Install Obsidian using Snap
docs.text:
1. Open your browser and go to Download Obsidian.
  2. Under Linux, click Snap to download the installation file.
  3. Open a terminal and navigate to the folder where you downloaded the installation file.
  4. In the terminal, run the following command to install the Snap package: (the --dangerous flag is required because Canonical, the company who created Snap, didn't review our package, the --classic flag allows Obsidian to access outside of the sandbox, where your notes are stored)

snap install obsidian_<version>_<arch>.snap --dangerous --classic

  1. Open Obsidian the same way you would open any other application.

docs.title: Install Obsidian using AppImage
docs.text:
1. Open your browser and go to Download Obsidian.
  2. Under Linux, click AppImage to download the installation file.
  3. Open a terminal and navigate to the folder where you downloaded the installation file.
  4. In the terminal, run the following command to open Obsidian:
chmod u+x Obsidian-<version>.AppImage
./Obsidian-<version>.AppImage --no-sandbox

Note: On Chromebooks, the libnss3-dev package must be installed or you may receive the error error while loading shared libraries: libnss3.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory.

docs.title: Install Obsidian using Flatpak
docs.text:
1. In your terminal, run the following command to install Obsidian:
flatpak install flathub md.obsidian.Obsidian
  1. Open Obsidian by running the following command: flatpak run md.obsidian.Obsidian

docs.title: Install Obsidian on Android
docs.text:
1. Find Obsidian on the Play Store.
  2. Tap Install to download the app.
  3. Open Obsidian the same way you would open any other app.

You can optionally download the APK for Android from the Download Obsidian page.

docs.title: Install Obsidian on iPhone and iPad
docs.text:
1. Find Obsidian on the App Store.
  2. Tap Get to download the app.
  3. Open Obsidian the same way you would open any other app.
